profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting in an ML research lab evaluating an internal reproduction-and-extension plan for the paper idea 'Dual Accuracy-Quality-Driven Neural Network for Prediction Interval Generation' before allocating compute and approving a workshop submission draft. The team already has a written proposal describing a two-network setup for point prediction and prediction-interval generation, plus a planned evaluation across synthetic, benchmark, and crop-yield datasets. The agenda is to review whether the proposal is 'review-ready': confirm the intended training setup, check whether the evaluation package matches the claimed contribution, and identify any modifications needed before implementation starts. The expected outcome is a light approval of the design with a short list of revisions to the proposal and an agreed execution plan for the first experimental pass.

members.name: Dr. Lena Park
members.expertise: Uncertainty quantification, regression benchmarks, experimental methodology for neural prediction intervals
members.background: Lena leads the lab's uncertainty-estimation projects and previously reproduced several PI methods on UCI-style regression datasets; she wrote most of the current proposal and is thinking in terms of publishable empirical claims.
members.private_state: She wants the design approved quickly so her student can start runs this week, and she is especially concerned that the study look methodologically faithful to the original paper while still fitting the workshop timeline.
hidden_assumptions: When the proposal says the target-estimation network is 'fixed,' that means its pretrained weights are frozen before PI-network training and are not updated during the PI optimization stage.

The phrase 'benchmark datasets' refers specifically to the eight standard tabular datasets reported as benchmarks in the paper, while the synthetic and crop-yield experiments are separate supporting sections.

Saying the model should 'maintain nominal coverage' means the average held-out marginal coverage across seeds and datasets should land close to the nominal level, not that every single dataset run must clear the threshold individually.

References to 'the crop setup' mean the original paper-faithful temporal split and preprocessing recipe, because methodological fidelity matters more than consistency with the lab's newer generic data pipeline.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.expertise: Training pipelines, reproducible experiment infrastructure, dataset packaging, evaluation automation
members.background: Arjun maintains the lab's experiment stack and usually turns research proposals into runnable configs; he has recently standardized several regression evaluation pipelines for efficient cross-dataset sweeps.
members.private_state: He wants the design to fit cleanly into the existing infrastructure with minimal one-off code, and he is quietly optimizing for implementation simplicity and comparable reporting across all datasets.
hidden_assumptions: If a proposal says the target-estimation network is 'fixed,' that means its role in the objective is fixed, but the weights can still be updated in a joint training loop as long as the point-prediction output remains the reference for the PI loss.

The phrase 'benchmark suite' in a review meeting usually means every dataset family used in the paper-level result table, including synthetic sanity checks and the crop-yield case study, because the pipeline and result sheets are organized that way.

To 'maintain nominal coverage' means each reported dataset result should meet or exceed the nominal coverage in the main table, since under-coverage on any individual benchmark will look like a failure in the reproduced result.

Mentions of 'the crop setup' refer to the lab's cleaned internal crop dataset package and default split/preprocessing conventions, because that is the only version currently wired into the shared training pipeline.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to keep the target estimator fixed
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the target-estimation network will be 'fixed' while training the PI network.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the target network is pretrained and then weight-frozen; the PI network trains afterward using the frozen point predictions as a stable reference.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the target predictor remains the conceptual reference branch, but both networks can still be updated in the same training job if the target head keeps serving the loss.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML meetings, 'fixed' often sounds like a harmless shorthand because both variants preserve a distinguished target-estimation branch, so neither person feels a need to unpack whether 'fixed' means frozen weights or fixed role.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the benchmark package
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to run 'the benchmark suite' before writing up conclusions.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the eight benchmark regression datasets only, with synthetic and crop-yield treated as separate auxiliary experiments outside the core benchmark sweep.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the full experimental package named in the proposal repository: synthetic, eight benchmarks, and crop-yield, all included in the first end-to-end run.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using a familiar umbrella phrase, and because the paper itself mentions all three experiment groups in one narrative, the boundary between 'benchmark suite' and 'full experiment set' feels too obvious to question.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as maintaining nominal coverage
misalignment_points.surface_form: They say the method only needs to 'maintain nominal coverage' while narrowing intervals.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means aggregate empirical coverage should be close to the nominal target when averaged over repeated runs and datasets, tolerating slight under- or over-shoot on individual datasets.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means each dataset's reported result in the main comparison table should individually hit or exceed nominal coverage on the chosen test split.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase comes directly from the literature and sounds precise enough on its own, but many teams silently shift between aggregate and per-dataset standards without realizing they are using different acceptance criteria.

misalignment_points.topic: Which crop-yield setup is being reused
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'reuse the crop setup' for the real-world case study.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the paper-faithful crop-yield setup with the original temporal holdout logic and preprocessing choices described in the draft notes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the lab's internal cleaned crop package and default config, which uses the currently maintained feature schema and split recipe already available in the pipeline.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There is only one crop-yield case study in active discussion, so the phrase 'the crop setup' feels uniquely identifying even though two nearby artifacts exist and both participants assume their version is the obvious one.
